item.title: Tralee school welcomes home student who won this year's Young Scientist Exhibition
item.description: Tributes are being paid to the Kerry student who won the 2026 Stripe Young Scientist & Technology Exhibition. Mercy Mounthawk student, 15-year-old, Aoibheann Daly scooped the top prize for her project, GlioScope. It’s designed to help doctors improve the treatment of brain cancer, and reduce the need for invasive biopsies. item.title: Public warned to remain vigilant about WhatsApp and Revenue scams
item.description: Gardaí are urging the public to remain vigilant regarding mobile phone scams, particularly on WhatsApp. People are advised to never send codes to known contacts when messaged on the platform. Sending these codes allows online scammers to hack and take over a person's WhatsApp account. item.title: Investigation into animal cruelty in Killarney after horse injured in sulky race
item.description: An investigation into animal cruelty in Killarney is underway after a horse was left badly injured following a sulky race on Saturday. The incident happened on the main Killarney to Fossa road at around lunchtime, and the horse was brought for treatment. The animal was said to be in a serious, exhausted state and is now in the care of the ISPCA. item.title: Body of woman recovered from River Feale
item.description: A woman's body has been recovered from the River Feale in the Killocrim area. The alarm was raised around 6 o'clock yesterday evening, following reports of a person in the water. A multi agency operation commenced, with members of Ballybunion Sea and Cliff Rescue, Listowel Fire Service and the Coast Guard, as well as local Gardaí. item.title: McGrath Cup final fixed for Saturday in Killarney
item.description: The McGrath Cup football final has been fixed for Saturday at 1:30. Fitzgerald Stadium Killarney will host the clash of Kerry and Cork. The details have been confirmed for Friday's O'Byrne Cup Football final. Advertisement Kildare will welcome Westmeath to St Conleth's Park in Newbridge for a half-seven throw-in. Westmeath will be hoping to land pre-season silverware under their new boss Mark McHugh, while Kildare are aiming to win the competition for a record 12th time.

item.title: United close to appointing Michael Carrick
item.description: Manchester United are close to appointing Michael Carrick as their caretaker head coach until the end of the season. item.title: Former Ulster lock joins Ireland coaching team
item.description: Former Ulster lock Alan O'Connor has joined the Ireland women's rugby coaching team ahead of the Six Nations. Erin King and Dorothy Wall are part of a 37-player squad for a training camp in Dublin this week. Both missed last summer's World Cup through injury, while Aoife Wafer has shaken off a shoulder issue to link up with the group. Advertisement

item.title: Mark Allen books place in quarter-finals at Masters
item.description: Antrim's Mark Allen has booked a place in the quarter-finals of snooker's Masters. He won five frames in a row to see off fellow former winner Mark Williams by six frames to two. Advertisement

item.title: Cobden to become main jockey for McManus
item.description: Harry Cobden will become the main jockey for owner JP McManus in both Ireland and Britain later this year. The 2024 British champion jockey is currently Paul Nicholls' stable rider and he'll begin his new role in May. Cobden says it's a "massive opportunity" for the coming seasons and he's looking forward to riding more regularly in Ireland. Advertisement
